output.brief: The August dip was mainly a cooling failure, not a housekeeping or kiosk problem. A chiller serving floors 6-8 failed on 4 August and wasn't fixed until 19 August. Rooms ran at 26-29°C. Room comfort on those floors fell from 8.4 to 6.1, and their overall score fell from 8.6 to 7.4. Scores recovered to 8.4-8.6 once cooling returned. Floors 1-5 held steady. Cleanliness scores and inspection pass rates were flat, and kiosk complaints and check-in scores did not move. The survey method didn't change. So I would not serve notice on Orrin, and I would not pull the kiosks. Don't drop the floor 6-8 responses from the reported score either. That would hide a real guest experience problem. I would do this next: restore the deferred chiller maintenance, keep critical spares on site, and write a recovery protocol for cooling outages. A further return-stay offer is reasonable, since guests already received an apology and half-night credit. The rate rise may have added a little to the value-score drop on floors 1-5. The data can't separate it from the usual August dip, so hold off reversing it and keep watching. I'm fairly confident in this diagnosis, with the rate-rise question the main unresolved point.
